findings.finding: Three stories describe the existence check with three different interaction models: an async ACK plus a later callback, a synchronous 200 with a boolean, and a Contract Manager call to an EDC endpoint. The live criteria also place the check on different sides.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-19824/AC1: 'the system returns an ACK (acknowledge) message with HTTP status code 200 (OK)' ... 'the system sends a response to the dedicated endpoint' (endpoint POST /agreements/{contractNegotiationId}/search). SIMPL-32509/AC1: 'the Provider invokes the POST /resourceDescriptions/{resourceDescriptionId}/validateExistenceContract API' ... 'Exists (boolean)' (path not in any OpenAPI). SIMPL-35858: 'As a Contract Manager on consumer side ... inform EDC whether an active contract already exists', AC1 'the CM sends a POST request to ... /isPresent/{contractNegotiationId}/{isPresent}'. BP7.2.2: 'A Provider verifies existence of a usage contract'.
findings.question: Which model is the target for the existence check: the existing async search endpoint with a callback, the new synchronous validateExistenceContract endpoint, or the /isPresent callback to EDC; and on which side (Provider or Consumer) does the Contract Manager run it?
options: Async: POST /agreements/{contractNegotiationId}/search returns an ACK, result reported to EDC via /isPresent (SIMPL-19824 + SIMPL-35858)
Sync: POST /resourceDescriptions/{resourceDescriptionId}/validateExistenceContract returns 200 with exists (SIMPL-32509), no callback

findings.finding: The create endpoint is assigned to the Provider in two stories and the process, and moved to the Consumer side in a third. The response also differs: an ACK with a later callback, a full offer body, or a 201 that triggers the Contract UI backend.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-19829/AC1 and SIMPL-32511 'As a Provider, I want to create a usage contract offer' on POST /credentials/agreements/{contractAgreementId}/definitions/{contractDefinitionId}/create; BP7.3.1 'A Provider creates the usage contract offer'. SIMPL-35526 'As a EDC connector on the consumer side', technical notes: 'Execute on the consumer side instead of the provider side', 'Do not call EDC callback endpoint afterwards', 'Call the Contract UI backend to store the prepared data (POST /contractOffers/{contractNegotiationId})'.
findings.question: On which side does /create run, and what does it return: ACK plus callback to the Provider Connector (SIMPL-19829), the offer body with usageContract and usageContractHash (SIMPL-32511), or 201 with a push to the Contract UI backend and a user notification (SIMPL-35526)?
options: Provider side, creates the offer and returns it (SIMPL-19829 / SIMPL-32511, BP7.3.1)
Consumer side, prepares offer data for the UI and notifies the user (SIMPL-35526)

findings.finding: Validation and Provider signing are specified twice with different observable outcomes. The older stories say validation is asynchronous and checked through persisted state and logs; the newer ones return 201 after validating and signing, or call EDC /isValid. SIMPL-19934 expects 200 with 'Finalized' from a signing call.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-19933/AC10: 'the final validation result is not expected to be returned synchronously in the triggering request'. SIMPL-35584/AC1: POST .../validateAndIssue 'returns a 201 Created response' 'And the VC from the consumer side is validated' 'And the contract is signed on the provider side'. SIMPL-19934/AC1: 'the system returns HTTP 200 (OK) with status "Finalized"'. SIMPL-21948/AC10 (async, persisted) versus SIMPL-35677/AC1 ('the EDC endpoint /isValid/{contractNegotiationId}/true is called').
findings.question: Which stories define the target validation and signing flow on each side, and which ones are superseded? What does a test observe: the HTTP response, the persisted state, or the EDC callback?
options: New flow: SIMPL-35584 (Provider) and SIMPL-35677 (Consumer) with EDC callbacks; SIMPL-19933, 19934, 21948 describe the same steps and only add the rejection reasons
Old flow: SIMPL-19933, 19934, 21948 stay normative; SIMPL-35584 and 35677 only add the EDC trigger

findings.finding: Each story uses its own set of status names for the same offer or contract, and the two APIs use yet other enums. A UI overview, a filter and the scheduler cannot be built without one agreed set and a mapping.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-30959/AC1 'Status (Requested, Rejected, Accepted, Signed, Active)'; SIMPL-21924/AC2 'status "In progress"'; SIMPL-32511/AC1 "status: 'Requested'"; SIMPL-32505/AC3 'accepted, active, rejected, suspended or terminated'; SIMPL-35692/AC4 'status Terminated', AC1 'pending'; SIMPL-31053/AC2 'Revocation requested'; SIMPL-31115/AC2 'Suspended'; SIMPL-31116/AC2 'Reactivation requested'; SIMPL-19934/AC1 'Finalized'. contract-ui-be ContractOffer.status enum CREATED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED; contract-manager-be ContractOffer.status CREATED, APPROVED, REJECTED; ConfirmationResponse.status INITIATED, CREATED, FINALIZING, FINALIZED, TERMINATED.
findings.question: What is the one status set for a usage contract offer and a usage contract (including Suspended, Revocation requested, Revoked, Reactivation requested, Terminated), and how does each map to the API enums?

findings.finding: The lifecycle stories (revoke, respond, suspend, reactivate, terminate) need operations that no OpenAPI offers, and each has a criterion where the other party sees the new status. No story says how the change reaches the other participant.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31053/AC3 'the requesting Participant has requested the revocation ... I can observe that the status ... has changed to 'Revocation requested''; SIMPL-31076/AC4.1, SIMPL-31115/AC3, SIMPL-31116/AC3, SIMPL-31117/AC3, SIMPL-31118/AC3 (same pattern). contract-ui-be offers only GET/POST/PATCH on /contractOffers with operation enum accept, reject; contract-manager-be has no revoke, suspend, reactivate or terminate operation. inventory-review.md: these criteria have 'no operation and no requirement'.
findings.question: Which backend owns the lifecycle state and operations (contract-manager-be or contract-ui-be), and through which channel (EDC, Kafka, other) is a status change passed to the other participant?

findings.finding: The wallet failure criteria ask the user to name another secure location, but storage happens inside an automatic backend flow with no user in the loop. A builder can read this as a UI prompt or as a failed step with an error.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-19927/AC2 'I receive an error message stating "Secure storage location unavailable" And I am requested to specify another secure location for archiving the contract'; same in AC3, AC4 and SIMPL-19938/AC2.1 to AC4.2. SIMPL-35584 technical description: 'Store the VC in the wallet service' inside the EDC-triggered handler; SIMPL-19934: 'Human UI interaction is not required.'
findings.question: When the wallet is unavailable, full or corrupted during the automatic signing flow, what happens: a user prompt for another location, or the step fails, the error is logged and EDC is told (for example /signed/{id}/false)? What does 'another secure location' mean, if anything?
options: UI prompt to choose another storage location (as written)
No prompt: the flow fails with an error, the contract is not finalised and EDC is informed

findings.finding: The story holds two live versions of AC1 to AC4 with different actors and outcomes. A builder does not know which version counts.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-19938/AC1.1 'Given that I am authenticated as a Provider ... And I digitally sign the usage contract ... Then I store securely'; SIMPL-19938/AC1.2 'Given a fully signed usage contract is received by the Provider ... Then the contract is securely stored ... And the contract is retrievable via Contract Manager API'. Same pattern for AC2 to AC4.
findings.question: Which version of AC1 to AC4 is the live one: the user-driven list items (AC1.1 to AC4.1) or the system-level headings (AC1.2 to AC4.2)?
options: List-item version (AC1.1, AC2.1, AC3.1, AC4.1)
Heading version (AC1.2, AC2.2, AC3.2, AC4.2)

findings.finding: The criterion expects the user to see the result of the access-policy and existence checks right after clicking, but the story's own technical description says the UI only starts the negotiation and does not poll. The checks run later at the Provider.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-21924/AC2 'Then I see the result of the positive validation of the usage contract offer request ... And A usage contract with the status "In progress" is created'. Technical Description: 'the Catalogue UI shall invoke the startNegotiation API and, upon receiving a successful response, update the negotiation status accordingly without triggering any polling process'. SIMPL-19824/AC1: async search with ACK. Same issue for AC3 and AC4 (errors shown by the catalogue UI).
findings.question: Does the catalogue UI show the validation result (positive, access denied, contract exists), or only that the request was sent, with the result shown later in the contract manager UI?
options: The UI waits for or polls the Provider checks and shows the result (AC2 to AC4 as written)
The UI shows 'request sent' only; results appear later in the contract manager UI

findings.finding: The only criterion has no oracle: no endpoint, no format, no 'given moment', and the 'audit rule package' from the user story is not described anywhere.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-34633/AC1 'Then the contract manager produces the usage contract audit And makes it available through an endpoint for the logging & monitoring component'. Note: 'the amount of usage contracts per status at a given moment'. User story: 'according to a supplied audit rule package'. No such endpoint in contract-manager-be.
findings.question: What is the endpoint and response format of the audit data, which status set is counted, what is 'a given moment' (on request, scheduled), and what is the audit rule package?

findings.finding: The story calls the accept and reject operation with POST and expects 201, while contract-manager-be defines PATCH /contractOffers/{contractNegotiationId}/{operation} returning 200. Tests from the story and a build from the API will disagree.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-35660/AC1 'sends a POST request to the API endpoint /contractOffers/{contractNegotiationId}/{operation} with the accept operation Then the API returns a 201 Created response'. contract-manager-be: 'PATCH /contractOffers/{contractNegotiationId}/{operation}' responses 200 'Transfer initiated', 400, 401, 403, 405, 406, 415, 500. inventory-review.md row e flags the method mismatch.
findings.question: Is the operation PATCH with 200 (as in the OpenAPI) or POST with 201 (as in the story)?
options: PATCH, 200 (OpenAPI)
POST, 201 (story)

findings.finding: The story calls /verifications with POST and expects '202 Created'; the OpenAPI defines PUT returning 200 with a VC in the request body. The story also says the Contract Manager fetches the VC itself through EDC, so the body may not be needed.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-35677/AC1 'the EDC sends a POST request to the API endpoint /verifications/{contractNegotiationId} Then the API returns a 202 Created response'. Technical Description: 'Get the providers VC using the new EDC endpoint'. contract-manager-be: 'PUT /verifications/{contractNegotiationId}', requestBody VerifyCredentialRequest, response 200 VerificationConfirmationResponse.
findings.question: Which method and status code apply (PUT/200, POST/201 or POST/202), and does EDC still send the VC in the body or does the Contract Manager fetch it via /vcExchange?
options: PUT, 200, VC in body (OpenAPI)
POST, 202 Accepted, no body, VC fetched via EDC (story)

findings.finding: The story has no criterion for the main failure: the consumer VC is invalid or cannot be fetched. A builder must guess whether the call returns an error code, returns 201 and reports false to EDC, or stays pending.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-35584 has AC1 (success, 201), AC2 (401), AC3 (400 on consumer side) only. Technical Description: 'Get the VC from the consumer using the new EDC endpoint', 'Technical validation', 'Business validation', 'Inform EDC by calling the sign endpoint'. SIMPL-35863 offers /isValid/{contractNegotiationId}/{isValid} 'on consumer or provider side'. SIMPL-19933/AC2 to AC9 list rejection reasons for the same step.
findings.question: What does validateAndIssue return and do when the consumer VC fails technical or business validation, when the VC cannot be fetched via EDC, and when the Signer, VC Issuer or wallet fails?
options: Synchronous error code (4xx or 5xx), contract not signed
201 accepted, then EDC is told via /isValid/{id}/false or /signed/{id}/false

findings.finding: The validation rules are delegated to an upload API that is not in the input set, and the story itself lists format, size, endpoint and errors as still to be clarified. A tester cannot write the pass or fail case for AC1 and AC3.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-28846/AC1 'validates the document against the supported document format, MIME type and file size rules defined by the upload API implementation'. AC3 same rules. Dependencies: 'The upload API definition must clarify: endpoint path and method, ... supported MIME types, maximum file size, validation errors'. No upload operation in contract-manager-be or contract-ui-be.
findings.question: Which upload operation, supported MIME types and maximum file size apply, and which component exposes the upload?

findings.finding: The success outcome of both validation stories is 'updated according to the agreed lifecycle' without naming the status, and the technical-error case allows two end states. There is no pass condition on the main path.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-19933/AC1 'the contract negotiation status is updated according to the agreed lifecycle'; SIMPL-21948/AC1 'the contract status is updated according to the agreed lifecycle'; SIMPL-19933/AC8 and SIMPL-21948/AC8 'the validation result is marked as failed or remains pending according to the agreed lifecycle'. SIMPL-21948 table: 'Contract marked as validated / finalized according to lifecycle', 'FAILED / PENDING_RETRY'.
findings.question: Which status does the negotiation or contract get after a successful validation, and after a technical error: FAILED or PENDING_RETRY (with retry)?
options: Technical error ends in FAILED
Technical error ends in PENDING_RETRY and is retried

findings.finding: The failure criteria say 'rejected or failed' without saying which, and only the Consumer-side story maps cases to reason codes. The Provider side has no codes.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-19933/AC2 'the validation result is marked as rejected or failed ... the rejection reason indicates invalid Consumer signature' (same in AC3 to AC6, AC9); SIMPL-21948/AC2 to AC9 same wording; SIMPL-21948 technical info table: 'REJECTED / FAILED', 'INVALID_PROVIDER_SIGNATURE', ... SIMPL-19933 has no table.
findings.question: Which value (REJECTED or FAILED) belongs to each case, and do the Provider-side reasons use the same codes as the SIMPL-21948 table (with CONSUMER instead of PROVIDER)?

findings.finding: Both validation stories check a validity period, but no API schema or story defines where an offer or contract carries its validity dates.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-19933/AC1 'the contract offer is within its validity period'; SIMPL-19933/AC4 'the contract offer validity period is outside the allowed timeframe'; SIMPL-21948/AC1, AC4 same. ContractOffer, ContractAgreementCreate and ContractAgreementData have no validity fields.
findings.question: Which field or rule defines the validity period of an offer and of a contract?

findings.finding: Duplicate or replayed submissions must be detected, but the key is not named. Two builders will pick different keys (negotiation id, signature, payload hash).
findings.evidence: SIMPL-19933/AC7 'When the same signed contract offer is received again ... the duplicate or replayed submission is detected'; SIMPL-21948/AC7 same; SIMPL-21948 table 'REJECTED / IGNORED'.
findings.question: What makes two submissions 'the same' (contractNegotiationId, signature value, payload hash), and is the result REJECTED or IGNORED?

findings.finding: 'Active usage contract' decides whether a new offer may be created, but the lifecycle stories add Suspended, Revocation requested and Reactivation requested. It is not said whether these count as active.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-32509 user story 'verify if the Consumer already has an active usage contract'; SIMPL-21924/AC4 'I already have an active usage contract'; SIMPL-19824/AC2 'an active contract exists'. SIMPL-31115/AC2 'Suspended', SIMPL-31053/AC2 'Revocation requested'.
findings.question: Which statuses count as 'active' for the existence check?

findings.finding: Consumer signing is described in three places with different triggers: a generic 'signing process is triggered', the accept operation on the Contract Manager, and the UI accept action. It is unclear whether SIMPL-21928 adds behaviour beyond SIMPL-35660.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-21928/AC1 'When the signing process is triggered Then Contract Manager completes the Consumer signing process'; SIMPL-35660/AC1 'with the accept operation ... the contract is signed on the consumer side'; SIMPL-32505/AC2 'I see the usage contract with the updated status "Accepted"'.
findings.question: Is SIMPL-35660 the concrete trigger for SIMPL-21928, so that accept means sign at once, or is signing a separate user step after accept?
options: Accept triggers signing at once (SIMPL-35660)
Accept and sign are separate steps

findings.finding: Two Contract Manager endpoints in the criteria are not in the OpenAPI, so request body, response body and error codes are unknown.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-35440/AC1 'GET /verifications/{contractNegotiationId}/vc'; SIMPL-35584/AC1 'POST ... /validateAndIssue' with 'Dependencies: SIMPL-35587 (API definition)'. inventory-review.md: 'Endpoints named in stories that are not in the three OpenAPI files'.
findings.question: Where are these two operations defined (request and response schema, error codes), and will they be added to contract-manager-be openapi3-v1.yaml?

findings.finding: Four stories specify endpoints of the EDC connector, not of the Contract Management component. For this component they only define the client side of a call.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-35858/AC1 'the EDC API accepts the contract existence result'; SIMPL-35863/AC1 'the EDC API accepts the validation result'; SIMPL-35888/AC1 'EDC retrieves the VC from the other participant's EDC'; SIMPL-35889 'this task extends the EDC API' (no acceptance criteria). SIMPL-35584 Dependencies: 'EDC VC exchange endpoint ... (Connector team)'.
findings.question: Are these stories in scope for the Contract Management build, or only as an interface contract the Contract Manager calls?
options: In scope: build them here
Out of scope: treat as the interface the Contract Manager calls

findings.finding: The lifecycle stories say why (remove or restore access) but no criterion says what happens to resource access, or who enforces it, when a contract becomes Suspended, Revoked, Terminated or Active again.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31115 'So that I have the flexibility to temporarily remove access to a resource'; SIMPL-31118 'So that I can remove access to a resource'; SIMPL-31117 'make the resource available again'. The Thens only check the status: SIMPL-31115/AC2 'status ... changed to 'Suspended''.
findings.question: Must the Contract Manager tell another component (connector, consumption adapter) about a status change so that access is removed or restored, and how is that observed?

findings.finding: Reasons and justifications are asked for in five actions, but no criterion says whether they are mandatory, what limits apply, or whether the other party sees them.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31053/AC1 'I am requested to provide a reason'; SIMPL-31076/AC3 'I provide a justification for the denial'; SIMPL-31115/AC2 'I provide a reason for the suspension'; SIMPL-31116/AC2 'I provide a justification'; SIMPL-31118/AC2 'I provide a justification related to the termination conditions'.
findings.question: Is the reason mandatory (and what happens if it is empty), is there a length limit, and is it shown to the other participant?

findings.finding: The 'securely stored' outcomes have no oracle beyond the wallet call, and 'access is restricted to authorized roles' names no role.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-19927/AC1 'Then I store securely the fully-signed usage contract in my digital wallet ... And its access is restricted to authorized roles'; SIMPL-19938/AC1.1 same; SIMPL-19938/AC1.2 'the contract is securely stored in the Provider digital wallet'.
findings.question: What does a test check for 'securely stored' (VC present in the wallet, retrievable via GET /agreements/{contractAgreementId}?), and which roles may read it?

findings.finding: One story forbids an 'unsigned VC' as an intermediate artefact while another describes one as a step. Signer naming also differs.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-21928: 'This story must not assume an "unsigned VC" as a formal intermediate artefact.' SIMPL-19934: 'the Contract Manager requests the VC Issuer Service to create an unsigned Signature VC', 'Digital Signature Service'; SIMPL-35584/35660: 'Signer Service'.
findings.question: Is the unsigned Signature VC a defined artefact, and are 'Digital Signature Service' and 'Signer Service' the same service?

findings.finding: The EDC callback criteria do not name the response code for an accepted result.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-35858/AC1 'the EDC API accepts the contract existence result (asynchronous)'; SIMPL-35863/AC1 'the EDC API accepts the validation result'.
findings.question: Which status code does EDC return when it accepts the result (200, 202, 204)?

findings.finding: The replaced story is still live and holds requirements its replacement lacks: 400 and 405 handling, error logging, and 'the contract establishment process is prevented from proceeding'.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-19824/AC3 '400 (Bad Request) ... the error event is logged ... prevented from proceeding'; AC5 '405 (Method Not Allowed)'; AC6 '500 ... the contract negotiation process is halted'. SIMPL-32509 'Replaces SIMPL-19824' has 200, 404, 'appropriate error', 401, 403 only.
findings.question: Should SIMPL-19824 be closed, and do its 400, 405, logging and 'prevent proceeding' outcomes carry over to SIMPL-32509?

findings.finding: The replaced story is still live and holds error cases its replacement lacks: 400, 401, 405, 415, 500 and 'no contract offer is created'.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-19829/AC2 to AC6 (400, 401, 405, 415, 500, each 'And no contract offer is created'). SIMPL-32511 'Replaces SIMPL-19829' has 201, 403, 404 only; its change log says 'Response codes: Following is added: 403, 404'.
findings.question: Should SIMPL-19829 be closed, and do its error criteria (including 'no contract offer is created') carry over to SIMPL-32511?

findings.finding: The replaced story is still live and adds requirements its replacement lacks: a failure case, idempotency per contractNegotiationId, an immutable audit record and correlationId. Its criteria also point to an API (SIMPL-28977) that is not in the input.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-22690/AC2 'the acceptance process fails Then an error response is returned And the contract negotiation remains active'; Security: 'acceptance endpoint idempotent per contractNegotiationId', 'acceptance decision recorded immutably in audit log'; AC1.2 'using the API defined in SIMPL-28977', 'logged with sufficient technical details'. SIMPL-32505 'Replaces SIMPL-22690' has no failure criterion.
findings.question: Should SIMPL-22690 be closed, and do the failure case, idempotency and audit requirements carry over to SIMPL-32505? What does 'remains active' mean as a status?

findings.finding: The catch-all error criterion has no oracle: 'cannot be properly fulfilled' is not a condition, and the code is 'appropriate' with examples.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-32509/AC4 'And the request cannot be properly fulfilled Then an appropriate error response is returned (e.g. 400, 406, 415, 500)'.
findings.question: Which conditions map to 400, 406, 415 and 500 for this endpoint?

findings.finding: The 401 and 403 cases are about the Consumer's authentication and role, while the call is made by the Provider and the APIs use an API key. Whose credentials are checked is unclear. AC3 is also missing from the numbering.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-32509/AC5 'Given an unauthenticated Consumer ... When ... the Provider invokes the POST ... Then the request is rejected with a 401'; AC6 'without a role authorised to submit a usage contract offer request ... 403'. contract-manager-be security: ApiKeyAuth (X-Api-Key). Labels: AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6.
findings.question: Is 401/403 about the caller's API key or about the Consumer identity carried in the request, and which role is required?
options: Caller (EDC/Provider) API key
Consumer identity and role in the request

findings.finding: The response status 'Requested' is not a value of the response enum, and the added response fields are not yet in the OpenAPI. A typo 'proverId' and '201 Ok' would be copied into tests.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-32511/AC1 "status: 'Requested' (String)", 'proverId (String)', 'I receive a 201 Ok response', 'usageContractHash' (no type). contract-manager-be /create 201 ConfirmationResponse.status enum INITIATED, CREATED, FINALIZING, FINALIZED, TERMINATED.
findings.question: Which enum value is returned on creation, and is the field providerId?

findings.finding: The user notification has no channel or content, and the failure paths (Contract UI backend or catalogue unavailable, no user email) have no criterion.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-35526/AC1 'And the Consumer user is notified that a usage contract offer is available for review'. Technical notes: 'Collect the user email and notify the user', 'Call the Contract UI backend to store the prepared data'. Only AC2 (401) as a negative case.
findings.question: How is the user notified (Notification Service email, UI only), and what does /create return when the Contract UI backend call or the notification fails?

findings.finding: The reject criterion has no response code, signing failures have no criterion, and there is no criterion for a call on the provider side, although the handler acts 'only when called on the consumer side'.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-35660/AC3 'Then the contract is not signed And the EDC endpoint /signed/{contractNegotiationId}/false is called' (no status code). Technical details: 'should (only when called on the consumer side)'. SIMPL-35584/AC3 and SIMPL-35677/AC4 do have a 400 'called on the wrong side' case.
findings.question: What does the reject call return, what happens when Signer, VC Issuer or wallet fails, and is a provider-side call answered with 400 as in SIMPL-35584/AC3?

findings.finding: No criterion covers the VC fetch failing (EDC unreachable, other side returns 404 per SIMPL-35440/AC2), and AC3 gives no response code.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-35677 Technical Description 'Get the providers VC using the new EDC endpoint'. AC3 'the provider VC fails the technical or business validation Then the EDC endpoint /isValid/{contractNegotiationId}/false is called' (no status code). SIMPL-35440/AC2 '404 Not Found'.
findings.question: When the provider VC cannot be fetched, is that /isValid false, an error response, or a retry? Which code does the call return in AC3?

findings.finding: The 404 case covers 'not signed yet' only. An unknown contractNegotiationId and an unavailable wallet have no criterion, though the handler checks both.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-35440/AC2 'the participant didn't signt the contract yet, so VC is not stored in the wallet ... 404'. Technical details: 'Check whether the contractNegotiationId exists in the Contract Manager DB', 'Collect the VC ... from the wallet service'.
findings.question: What is returned for an unknown contractNegotiationId and when the wallet service is unavailable?

findings.finding: 'Pending' and 'finalized' are not values of the Contract UI backend status enum, so the scheduler's selection is open. 'Terminated' is also not in the enum. A failing reject call to the Contract Manager has no criterion.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-35692/AC1 'a pending contract offer'; AC3 'already finalized'; AC4 'shown with status Terminated'. Technical Description: 'contract offers in the Pending state', 'Mark it as terminated', 'Send a rejection request to the Contract Manager'. contract-ui-be ContractOffer.status enum CREATED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED.
findings.question: Which UI statuses are 'pending' (CREATED only, or CREATED and ACCEPTED) and 'finalized'? Is Terminated a new enum value? What happens if the reject call to the Contract Manager fails?
options: Pending = CREATED
Pending = CREATED or ACCEPTED (not yet signed)

findings.finding: The success response differs from the signing operation it links to: 200 in the story, 201 in the OpenAPI. The 'backend API' is not named.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-19934/AC1 'the system returns HTTP 200 (OK) with status "Finalized"'. contract-manager-be POST .../issue 'Issue Verifiable credential. Start the process of signing contract.' responses 201 ConfirmationResponse.
findings.question: Is the Provider signing call POST .../issue (201) or another operation, and is the returned status FINALIZED or FINALIZING?

findings.finding: The criteria describe abilities ('can access', 'can continue') and 'sufficient evidence' without an observable check. The story defers the mechanism to other stories.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-21963/AC1 'the Provider can access the Consumer-signed usage contract offer or signing evidence'; AC3 'cannot continue as successful'; AC4 'there is sufficient evidence to confirm'. Technical note: 'Evidence may be existing Contract API result, persisted backend state or logs'.
findings.question: Which observable item proves delivery (a status on GET /agreements/{contractAgreementId}, a PATCH .../status call, a log entry), and does this story add anything beyond SIMPL-35660 and SIMPL-35584?

findings.finding: The outcomes 'signing result is registered' and 'rejected' have no observable form: no status, no field, no response code.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-21928/AC1 'the signing result is registered for the usage contract offer'; AC2 'using the agreed backend signing flow'; AC3 'the signing request is rejected And the usage contract offer is not marked as signed'.
findings.question: Where is the signing result visible (status value, field), and what does a rejected request return (401, 403)?

findings.finding: The Provider must send an email to the Consumer, but the recipient is 'resolved from participant context' with no source for the address, and retry is deferred to a contract that is not in the input.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-21966/AC2 'the Consumer recipient context is resolved from the contract negotiation / participant context'; AC5 'handled according to the error handling / retry behaviour defined by the agreed Notification Service integration contract'; Technical Notes: 'defined under SIMPL-29268', 'Recipient contact details must not be hardcoded'.
findings.question: Where does the Provider get the Consumer email address, and what retry rule applies when the Notification Service rejects the message?

findings.finding: 'Clear' error messages have no oracle: no status code, no error format, no message text.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-28846/AC3 'returns a clear validation error'; AC4 and AC5 'returns a clear error message to the Provider user'.
findings.question: Which status codes and error format (for example RFC 9457 Problem) apply to validation, metadata and storage failures?

findings.finding: The main business object has four live names. The business process and the stories say 'usage contract'; the CDM, the API paths and schemas say 'contract agreement'; newer API stories say 'contract'; the dynamic view says 'Usage Contract Agreement'. A test writer working from the stories and a code writer working from the API will name the same thing differently.
findings.evidence: BP07 README: 'establish a legally binding usage contract'; 'usage contract' appears in 30+ stories (for example SIMPL-31053, 31115, 31118, 19927). CDM:contract-manager-be:ContractAgreement; contract-manager-be paths /agreements/{contractAgreementId}, schemas ContractAgreementData, ContractAgreementCreate, operation summary 'Get Contract Agreement'. SIMPL-35584 title 'Contract Manager validates and signs contract agreement'; SIMPL-21928 'based on a contract agreement'; SIMPL-35660 'the contract is signed on the consumer side'; SIMPL-21948 'the contract is not marked as successfully validated'. bp07-dynamic-view.md: 'Verifiable Credential (VC) for the Usage Contract Agreement'. CDM:consent-management-be:ContractAgreement references the same class.
findings.question: Which single term names the legally binding contract between Consumer and Provider, in the stories, the CDM class and the API schemas?
options: Proposed: 'usage contract' everywhere (business process and 30+ stories use it); rename the CDM class to UsageContract and treat ContractAgreement as a deprecated alias until the API moves
Keep 'contract agreement' in the CDM and the API, and record in the glossary that it is the technical name of 'usage contract' (weaker: DDD-01 asks for one term)
Rewrite the stories to 'contract agreement' (not proposed: against the business process)

findings.finding: 'Contract agreement' names two different concepts. The Contract Consumption CDM separates the EDC operational agreement (EDCContractAgreement) from the business ContractAgreement owned by the Contract Manager and says no identifier equivalence is implied. Yet the Contract Manager API is called by the EDC connector with a contractAgreementId in the path, so the same id appears to serve both. A builder cannot tell whether contractAgreementId is the EDC agreement id or a Contract Manager key.
findings.evidence: CDM:contract-consumption-adapter-be:EDCContractAgreement: 'operational agreement produced by EDC negotiation finalization, distinct from the business ContractAgreement owned by Contract Manager BE'; section 8: 'These are distinct concepts; no direct integration or identifier equivalence is implied.' CDM:contract-manager-be:ContractAgreement.contractAgreementId 'UUID PK'. SIMPL-35526/AC1: 'the EDC connector sends a POST request to the API endpoint /credentials/agreements/{contractAgreementId}/definitions/{contractDefinitionId}/create'. SIMPL-35584/AC1 same pattern for .../validateAndIssue. contract-consumption-adapter-be ContractNegotiation.contractAgreementId (EDC value).
findings.question: Is the Contract Manager's contractAgreementId the EDC agreement id, or its own key with a separate reference to the EDC agreement?
options: Same id: the usage contract is keyed by the EDC agreement id; then the Contract Consumption CDM's 'no identifier equivalence' note must change
Different ids: the Contract Manager mints its own usage contract id and stores the EDC agreement id as a reference (for example edcContractAgreementId); the API paths then need renaming

findings.finding: 'ContractOffer' names two different concepts. In the Contract Manager CDM it is an external class (the EDC contract offer, referenced by contractOfferId). In both APIs it is the human-readable presentation of the offer (HTML, hash, status), which the Contract UI CDM calls HumanReadableContractData. The usage contract offer of the business process is a third reading. Tests and code built from different sources will attach offer status to different objects.
findings.evidence: CDM:contract-manager-be:ContractOffer '<<external>>', relation 'ContractOffer "1" --> "0..*" ContractAgreement : is accepted as'; ContractAgreementData.contractOfferId. contract-manager-be#ContractOffer {humanReadable, hash, status CREATED/APPROVED/REJECTED}, operation 'Transfer contract offer presentation'. contract-ui-be#ContractOffer {humanReadable, hash, status CREATED/ACCEPTED/REJECTED}, operation 'Create contract offer presentation'. CDM:contract-ui-be:HumanReadableContractData {contractNegotiationId, humanReadableData, status, contractData}. BP7.3.1 'A Provider creates the usage contract offer'. SIMPL-19829/AC1 'a machine-readable usage contract offer ... is created in JSON format'.
findings.question: Are the EDC contract offer, the machine-readable usage contract offer and the human-readable offer presentation one concept or three, and which of them owns the offer status?
options: Proposed: three terms. 'usage contract offer' (business object with the status), 'human-readable usage contract offer' (its HTML rendering and hash, a value object), 'EDC contract offer' (external, contractOfferId only)
One concept 'usage contract offer' whose rendering is an attribute; drop HumanReadableContractData and mark the EDC offer as a reference only

findings.finding: The usage contract (and its offer) has no single identity. Offer, verification, VC and one search endpoint are keyed by contractNegotiationId; the agreement, credential and status endpoints by contractAgreementId. The same collection /agreements is addressed by a negotiation id in one path and an agreement id in another. The UI overview of usage contracts shows 'Contract negotiation ID' as the contract's id. The offer is created through a path that already requires a contractAgreementId, before any agreement exists.
findings.evidence: contract-manager-be: POST /agreements/{contractNegotiationId}/search and GET /agreements/{contractAgreementId}; /contractOffers/{contractNegotiationId}; PUT /verifications/{contractNegotiationId}; POST /credentials/agreements/{contractAgreementId}/definitions/{contractDefinitionId}/create. contract-ui-be: /contractOffers/{contractNegotiationId}. SIMPL-30959/AC1 overview columns 'Contract negotiation ID; Resource description ID; ...'. SIMPL-32511/AC1 '/credentials/agreements/{contractAgreementId}/.../create' then 'the usage contract offer overview is created'. SIMPL-35440 'GET /verifications/{contractNegotiationId}/vc'. CDM:contract-manager-be:ContractAgreement has both contractAgreementId (PK) and contractNegotiationId.
findings.question: Which identifier identifies a usage contract offer and the resulting usage contract over the whole lifecycle, and under which name do the APIs expose it?
options: One id for the whole lifecycle (for example contractNegotiationId from the first request), with contractAgreementId as an attribute set at finalisation

Two entities with two ids: usage contract offer keyed by contractNegotiationId, usage contract keyed by contractAgreementId, with a written link; then /agreements/{contractNegotiationId}/search and the offer-creating .../create path need new names

findings.finding: No lifecycle is defined once for the usage contract offer or the usage contract. The Contract Manager CDM types the status as ContractAgreementStatus but never lists its values; the Contract UI CDM has no value set at all (the values sit only in cdm.puml next to the API). The stories add Suspended, Revocation requested, Revoked, Reactivation requested and Terminated with transitions, and no API operation changes them. The 23a script found 18 value-set mismatches; they all trace back to this missing definition.
findings.evidence: CDM:contract-manager-be:ContractAgreement.status 'ContractAgreementStatus' (no value set in the CDM). CDM:contract-ui-be:HumanReadableContractData.status (no values); specs/api/contract-ui-be/cdm.puml 'Allowed statuses: CREATED (default) ACCEPTED REJECTED'. contract-manager-be ConfirmationResponse.status and ContractAgreementData.status INITIATED, CREATED, FINALIZING, FINALIZED, TERMINATED ('Status of the process'); StatusUpdate FINALIZED, TERMINATED. SIMPL-31053/AC2 'Revocation requested'; SIMPL-31076/AC2 'Revoked', AC3 'changed back to Active'; SIMPL-31115/AC2 'Suspended'; SIMPL-31116/AC2 'Reactivation requested'; SIMPL-31117/AC2 'Active'; SIMPL-31118/AC2 'Terminated'. 23a: 'Revocation requested' in 6 clauses, 'Reactivation requested' in 4, 'Requested' in 1, with no API or CDM value.
findings.question: Where is the one state machine for the usage contract offer and the usage contract written down (states, allowed transitions, who triggers each), and which operation performs each transition?
options: Proposed: one state machine for the usage contract in the Contract Manager CDM, with the offer states as its first phase (Requested, Accepted, Rejected, Signed) and the contract states after it (Active, Suspended, Reactivation requested, Revocation requested, Revoked, Terminated)
Two state machines: usage contract offer (in the Contract UI CDM) and usage contract (in the Contract Manager CDM), with the hand-over state named

findings.finding: The accepted offer has two values on the main path. The Contract UI backend stores ACCEPTED and forwards the decision to the Contract Manager, whose offer status enum has APPROVED instead. The stories say 'Accepted'. A builder of either side has to guess the translation.
findings.evidence: contract-ui-be#ContractOffer.status enum CREATED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED; PATCH description 'Capture user decision about ACCEPTED or REJECTED contract offer'. contract-manager-be#ContractOffer.status and #ContractOfferStatusUpdate.status enum CREATED, APPROVED, REJECTED. SIMPL-32505/AC2 'the updated status "Accepted"'; SIMPL-30959/AC1 'Status (Requested, Rejected, Accepted, Signed, Active)'. cdm.puml 'ACCEPTED'.
findings.question: Is the accepted state ACCEPTED or APPROVED in both APIs?
options: Proposed: ACCEPTED (stories, UI API, cdm.puml and the 'accept' operation all use it)
APPROVED in both

findings.finding: The UI labels for statuses have no written mapping to stored values. 'Requested', 'Signed' and 'Active' have no API value at all; 'Requested' also appears as an API response value in SIMPL-32511 while the enum says CREATED; 'In progress' is used for a newly created usage contract.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-30959/AC1 and SIMPL-30960/AC1 'Status (Requested, Rejected, Accepted, Signed, Active)'. SIMPL-32511/AC1 response "status: 'Requested' (String)". SIMPL-21924/AC2 'A usage contract with the status "In progress" is created'. SIMPL-35692/AC1 'pending contract offer', AC4 'shown with status Terminated'. contract-ui-be ContractOffer.status CREATED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED.
findings.question: For each UI label, which stored value does it show, and where is that mapping kept?
options: Use the stored values as labels (no mapping needed)
Keep business labels in the UI and add a mapping table to the glossary and the UI CDM

findings.finding: 'Terminated' means three different things: a usage contract ended by the Provider because its termination conditions are met; an unsigned offer closed by the scheduler after the timeout (which is sent on as a reject); and a contract negotiation that ended without agreement (API value TERMINATED, EDC state).
findings.evidence: SIMPL-31118/AC2 'the usage contract is terminated ... changed to Terminated'. SIMPL-35692/AC1 'the contract offer is terminated', Technical Description 'Send a rejection request to the Contract Manager /contractOffers/{contractNegotiationId}/reject'. SIMPL-35660/AC3 'so that EDC terminates the negotiation'. contract-manager-be StatusUpdate.status FINALIZED, TERMINATED. CDM:contract-consumption-adapter-be NegotiationState TERMINATED 'Negotiation ended without agreement'.
findings.question: Should an offer closed by timeout and a contract ended by the Provider carry different state names?
options: Proposed: 'Terminated' only for a usage contract ended by the Provider; 'Expired' (or 'Rejected' with reason timeout) for an offer closed by the scheduler; TERMINATED stays an EDC negotiation state
Keep 'Terminated' for both and add a reason field

findings.finding: 'Signed usage contract' is used for the offer signed only by the Consumer and for the contract signed by both. The business process keeps them apart ('signed usage contract offer' after the Consumer signs, 'signed usage contract' after the Provider signs), but SIMPL-19938 says the Provider receives 'a signed usage contract' from the Consumer.
findings.evidence: BP7.5.2 'stores the signed usage contract offer and provide it to the Provider'; BP7.7.2 'A Provider stores the signed usage contract'. SIMPL-19938/AC1.1 'I receive a signed usage contract from a Consumer And I digitally sign the usage contract'; AC5 'a usage contract is received by the Provider'. SIMPL-19927/AC1 'fully-signed usage contract'; SIMPL-19934/AC1 'the final contract signed by both parties'.
findings.question: Do the stories adopt the business process pair 'signed usage contract offer' (Consumer signature only) and 'signed usage contract' (both signatures)?
options: Proposed: yes; retire 'fully-signed usage contract' and 'final contract signed by both parties' as synonyms of 'signed usage contract'

findings.finding: The check of the other party's signed offer or contract is called 'validate' in the business process and most stories, and 'verify' in the API and SIMPL-35677, which implements BP 7.8.1. The business process uses 'verify' for a different step (access policy and existing contract, BP 7.2).
findings.evidence: BP7.6.1 'A Provider validates the signed usage contract offer'; BP7.8.1 'A Consumer validates the signed usage contract'; BP7.2.1 'verifies the access policies'; BP7.2.2 'verifies existence of a usage contract'. contract-manager-be PUT /verifications/{contractNegotiationId}, operationId contract#verifyCredential, VerificationConfirmationResponse. SIMPL-35677 title 'Contract Manager verify contract on consumer side', AC1 'the providers VC is verified'. SIMPL-21948/AC1 'the validation result is marked as successful'. SIMPL-35863 '/isValid/...'.
findings.question: Should the API resource and the stories use 'validation' for the signed offer and contract check, and keep 'verify' for the BP 7.2 checks?
options: Proposed: 'validate' / 'validation' for BP 7.6 and 7.8 (business process wording); 'verify' only for BP 7.2
Keep /verifications and record 'verification' as a synonym in the glossary

findings.finding: The resource a contract covers is identified by three different ids under three names: resourceDescriptionId in the stories and the UI overview, assetId in the Contract Manager API and CDM, and selfDescriptionId in SIMPL-35526. No source says how they relate, so the overview cannot show 'Resource description ID' for a contract stored with an assetId.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-30959/AC1 'Resource description ID'; SIMPL-32509/AC1 'resourceDescriptionId (UUID)'; SIMPL-19824 'resource description'. contract-manager-be ContractAgreementCreate.assetId, ContractAgreementData.assetId; CDM:contract-manager-be:Asset (external), ContractAgreement.assetId. SIMPL-35526 technical notes 'use selfDescriptionId instead of assetId + contractDefinitionId'. CDM:consent-management-be:ResourceDescription (owned by Federated Catalogue); CDM:contract-consumption-adapter-be:Dataset.assetId.
findings.question: Is the usage contract linked to the resource description (catalogue identity) or to the EDC asset, and under which name?
options: Proposed: reference the resource description by resourceDescriptionId (catalogue owns it); keep assetId only as the EDC reference
Keep assetId and document how a resource description id is derived from it

findings.finding: The Contract Manager CDM defines VerifiableCredential as its own class with its own attributes, while the Issuer Service CDM owns VerifiableCredential with different attributes and the Wallet CDM calls the stored object Credential. The API schema follows the W3C data model, which neither CDM matches. The class should be external and point to its owner.
findings.evidence: CDM:contract-manager-be:VerifiableCredential {credentialType, issuer, issuanceDate, validFrom, validUntil, credentialStatus, credentialSubject}, no <<external>> stereotype. CDM:issuer-service-be:VerifiableCredential {type[], issuanceDate, validity, schema}, CredentialStatusType ACTIVE, REVOKED, SUSPENDED. CDM:wallet-service-be:Credential {type, issuer}. contract-manager-be#VerifiableCredential '@context, id, type, name, description, issuer, issuanceDate, credentialSubject, validFrom, validUntil, credentialStatus, credentialSchema, refreshService, termsOfUse, evidence, proof' ('W3C Verifiable Credential').
findings.question: Should the Contract Manager CDM mark VerifiableCredential as external (owned by the VC Issuer) and keep only the reference it needs?
options: Proposed: yes, <<external>> VerifiableCredential owned by Issuer Service BE, with the relation 'usage contract is signed by'; no attributes redefined

findings.finding: The external classes of the Contract Manager CDM name no owner, and their names differ from the owners' CDMs: Asset (catalogue says ResourceDescription, the consumption CDM says Dataset), Provider and Consumer as classes (the owners model Participant with a role), ContractNegotiation and ContractDefinition (the consumption CDM names them EDCContractNegotiation and EDCContractDefinition, owned by the EDC Connector).
findings.evidence: CDM:contract-manager-be: ContractDefinition, ContractNegotiation, ContractOffer, Asset, Provider, Consumer, all '<<external>>' with no owner. CDM:contract-consumption-adapter-be: 'Participant | Identity Provider', 'PartyRole ... is an interaction role, not a Participant attribute', EDCContractNegotiation and EDCContractDefinition 'External, EDC Connector'. CDM:consent-management-be: Participant (Identity Provider), ResourceDescription (Federated Catalogue), PartyType PROVIDER, CONSUMER.
findings.question: Should the Contract Manager CDM reference external concepts by their owners' names and list each owner?
options: Proposed: Participant (Identity Provider) with roles Provider and Consumer; ResourceDescription (Federated Catalogue); EDC contract negotiation, definition and offer marked as EDC Connector references

findings.finding: The Contract Manager API speaks the EDC connector's language: its paths and payloads are keyed on contract negotiation, contract definition, asset and contract offer ids, and its info says it is for 'interaction with the Dataspace connector'. The translation to EDC also sits in two places: the stories have the Contract Manager call EDC endpoints directly, while SIMPL-22690 and flow.puml put a Contract Orchestrator and Kafka in between. The business process notes that negotiation of terms is not a current requirement, yet 'contract negotiation' is the main key.
findings.evidence: contract-manager-be info.description 'Contract Manager HTTP APIs for interaction with the Dataspace connector'; paths with {contractNegotiationId}, {contractDefinitionId}; ContractAgreementCreate {contractNegotiationId, assetId, providerId, consumerId, contractOfferId}. SIMPL-35660 'the EDC endpoint /signed is called'; SIMPL-35677 '/isValid/{contractNegotiationId}/true is called'; SIMPL-35584 'Inform EDC by calling the sign endpoint'. SIMPL-22690 'Contract UI Frontend -> Contract UI Backend -> Contract Backend -> Kafka -> Contract Orchestrator -> EDC'; flow.puml participants EDC, Contract orchestrator, Contract backend. BP07 README: 'usage contract term negotiation ... is not a current requirement'.
findings.question: Where is the one translation layer between Contract Management and the EDC connector (Contract Manager itself, or the Contract Orchestrator), and which business terms does the Contract Manager API use instead of EDC terms?
options: Proposed: one anti-corruption layer (the Contract Orchestrator, if it is kept) that maps EDC negotiation, agreement and asset ids to usage contract terms; the Contract Manager API then uses usage contract offer, usage contract and resource description
The Contract Manager is the translation layer; drop the Contract Orchestrator from the flow and record the EDC term mapping in its CDM

findings.finding: The usage contract offer is changed in two components with no named root. The Contract UI backend stores the offer and its status and takes the accept or reject decision; the Contract Manager has its own PATCH on the same path, a PUT that sets the offer status 'on UI side', and creates the offer through the agreement path. It is not said which component owns the offer aggregate.
findings.evidence: contract-ui-be POST, GET, PATCH /contractOffers/{contractNegotiationId}[/{operation}]. contract-manager-be POST /contractOffers/{contractNegotiationId} ('Transfers a contract offer presentation to contract-ui-backend'), PATCH /contractOffers/{contractNegotiationId}/{operation}, PUT /contractOffers/{contractNegotiationId}/update ('Get status update from provider side and transfer it to UI side'). CDM:contract-ui-be:HumanReadableContractData.status. SIMPL-35692 'Mark it as terminated in contract UI database' then reject via the Contract Manager.
findings.question: Which component is the root of the usage contract offer (holds its state and performs its transitions), and which only shows it?
options: Contract Manager owns the offer; the Contract UI backend keeps a read model
Contract UI backend owns the offer until acceptance; the Contract Manager owns the usage contract after it

findings.finding: Several business objects the stories rely on have no CDM class and no API schema: the validation result with its rejection reason, the revocation request with its reason, the suspension and reactivation reasons, the Contract Clause document with its hash metadata, the usage contract audit data and the notification request. The code writer will invent their names.

Rejection reason INVALID_PROVIDER_SIGNATURE ...'; SIMPL-19933/AC2 'the rejection reason indicates invalid Consumer signature'. findings.question: Which of these are Contract Management business objects that belong in its CDM, and which are owned elsewhere (Notification Service, document storage, logging and monitoring)?

findings.finding: The attributes of the human-readable offer have three sets of names: humanReadable and hash in both APIs, humanReadableData and contractData in the Contract UI CDM, and usageContract (html) and usageContractHash in the SIMPL-32511 response. The hash is one concept with two names.

findings.question: Which attribute names does the human-readable usage contract offer use in the CDM and both APIs?
options: Proposed: humanReadable and hash (already in both APIs); align the UI CDM and SIMPL-32511 to them
humanReadableContent and contentHash everywhere

findings.finding: Each API has a CDM in the register, but all three are 'In review, not approved for delivery'. The Contract Manager CDM has two own classes and the Contract UI CDM one, against about ten business objects in the stories. findings.finding: Two state-changing operations of the published API have no decision: build or retire. The decisions put Consumer signing inside the accept call (D5) and Provider signing inside validateAndIssue (D7), and treat the stories linked to these operations (SIMPL-19934, 21928, 21963) as superseded or made concrete elsewhere (D1). Yet the OpenAPI still offers /issue, which starts signing on its own, and PATCH .../status, which lets any caller with the API key set FINALIZED or TERMINATED directly. That bypasses the D12 state machine: Active is reached only through D7 or a successful D8 validation. One builder will implement them from the OpenAPI, another will leave them out, and the tests have no oracle for either.

Final step in the process', body StatusUpdate with enum [FINALIZED, TERMINATED] (line 1398). links.json links SIMPL-19934/AC1, AC2, SIMPL-21928/AC1, AC2 and SIMPL-21963/AC1 to /issue and SIMPL-21963/AC1 to /status. D12 lists the only allowed transitions.
findings.question: Are POST .../issue and PATCH .../status retired in the target design, or kept? If kept, which D12 transitions may they cause and on which side?
options: Retire both: not built, not in the next OpenAPI version (simplest, matches D5 and D7)
Keep /issue as an internal alias of the D5 or D7 signing step, and retire PATCH .../status
Keep both, guarded by D12: PATCH .../status only Signed to Active or Closed, with 409 otherwise

findings.finding: Four operations have no acceptance criterion and no decision. A builder working from the OpenAPI and a tester working from the decisions will disagree, and a contract-testing tool that checks responses against the OpenAPI will reject correct answers. The decisions already ask to add the three new operations (D7, D10, D17); they do not ask to add these codes to the existing ones.

findings.finding: Request schemas allow what the decisions forbid, or forbid what they allow. The search body and ContractAgreementCreate declare no required properties, while D3, D4 and D7 make all five fields required with a 400 otherwise.
